catalyst.event: POSITION UPDATE — opened 2026-08-22 at 115, last 120.26 (+4.6%). Driver is the re-rating of a reset earnings base: FY26 guidance is EPS 10.95-11.15 on sales 11.0-11.15B, cut from 12.10-12.30 in June. Q2 FY26 prints 09/03 after the close and is a binary event inside the long-term thesis, with the Q2 bar set by management at EPS 1.76-1.81 versus a 2.68 pre-cut consensus.
catalyst.action: HOLD the existing position and DO NOT add before the print. Re-accumulate after 09/03 only: first tranche 112-118 if FY guidance holds, second tranche under 105 if the market overshoots a soft quarter. Never average in ahead of the event.

thesis: At 120.26 LULU trades near 10.9x the low end of its own reset FY26 guidance of 10.95-11.15 EPS, a multiple normally reserved for a structurally broken retailer rather than a brand still earning 55%-plus gross margins with no meaningful net debt. The June cut already took the number down roughly 10 percent, so 09/03 is judged against a bar management set itself rather than the pre-cut consensus that drove the 42 percent year-to-date de-rating.
key_risk: The problem is demand-side, not cost-side — management blamed negative brand commentary and weak product launches — so a second consecutive guidance cut on 09/03 would confirm the de-rating is earnings-driven rather than multiple-driven. Positioning into the print is crowded: 08/31 traded 13.65M shares against a 4.2M average, which is how a miss gaps rather than drifts. Explicit invalidation: a second consecutive guidance cut, FY27 EPS guided below 9.00, or gross margin below 52 percent for two consecutive quarters; bear-case value 88 is 11x on 8.00 of EPS.
counter_argument: Athleisure brands rarely recover a premium multiple once the culture moves on — Under Armour spent a decade cheap and never re-rated. Buying 11x on the assumption the multiple returns is a bet on taste, and if North America comps stay negative alongside China softness, FY27 EPS toward 8.00 puts the stock at 88 with nothing structural underneath it.

catalyst.event: California SB 492 floor vote. Lawmakers amended the bill over the weekend to strip the three provisions Newsom wanted — a $6B per-incident cap on wildfire-fund withdrawals, a ban on insurer subrogation suits against utilities, and a mechanism to replenish the fund once depleted. PCG fell 20.1% to 13.27 on 154.0M shares (normal volume roughly 20M) and EIX fell 23.1% to 53.98. Wells Fargo cut to Equal Weight (PT 24 from 25), BMO to Market Perform (PT 21 from 28) — both targets still sit 58-81% above the close.
catalyst.action: WAIT for the vote. Do not catch this on day two of a 20% legislative gap. Buy only into the 11.40-13.00 zone after SB 492 is actually voted on, in one third-size tranche; add only if the passed text preserves the AB 1054 liability cap. If the fund is left uncapped AND unreplenished with no cap on utility liability, there is no trade here at any price.

thesis: PG&E reaffirmed FY26 non-GAAP core EPS guidance of $1.64-1.66 alongside a $73B capital plan to 2030, 9% annual rate-base growth, 9%-plus EPS growth for 2027-2030 and explicitly no equity dilution. At 13.27 the market pays 8.0x that reaffirmed number for a regulated monopoly that ordinarily clears 15-18x, so the 20% gap prices a step-change in liability exposure rather than the change in fund mechanics that actually occurred. The re-rating leg is arithmetic: 12x roughly $1.80 of 2027 EPS is $21.60, which is also where the two downgrading brokers set their cut targets.
key_risk: This is a conviction-2 lottery ticket and the thinness is the point: I cannot verify from public reporting whether the AB 1054 liability cap (20% of T&D equity rate base for a utility holding a valid safety certification) survives the amended SB 492 text, and that single question decides whether the equity is cheap or impaired. PG&E must fund roughly 48% of the state wildfire fund with costs it cannot pass to customers, the fund no longer replenishes, and insurers can still subrogate. This company already wiped out its equity in the 2019 bankruptcy on precisely this mechanism, and no insider has bought a share on the open market in six months — 0 buys against 9 sales worth $6.36M.
counter_argument: The market moved $6B of PG&E market value and $8B-plus across PCG and EIX together in one session on a bill text professionals read in full; assuming a 20% repricing by utility specialists is an overreaction because two sell-side targets lag by a day is the weakest form of value investing. A single bad fire season now depletes a non-replenishing fund and returns PG&E to uncapped exposure, in which case the equity is worth its stub value, not 12x anything, and the 9.50 bear case is itself generous.

catalyst.event: Renewed US-Iran strikes on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz (08/30) pushed Brent to $90.91 (+3.2%) on 08/31, re-tightening the jet fuel input after UAL had already cut FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $7-11 from $12-14 on roughly $6B of added fuel expense. Alaska has withdrawn 2026 guidance outright and Delta has pulled back current-quarter capacity on $2B-plus of added cost. September is seasonally the weakest revenue month of the airline year, and Q3 results land mid-October against a fuel assumption set before this escalation.
catalyst.action: Short into strength only — sell the 111-118 retest of the broken 20-day (120.47) and 50-day (123.05) averages. Do NOT chase the break: UAL closed 107.99 sitting directly on its 200-day SMA at 108.03, and initiating here means a stop through the whole bounce. Cover half at 92.

thesis: US jet fuel is running near $4.88/gal, about $205/bbl, and the 08/30 Hormuz escalation reprices the input above the assumption behind UAL guidance that was already cut once. The stock has printed five consecutive down days (117.41, 114.83, 112.39, 110.60, 107.99) into its 200-day SMA at 108.03, so the trend and the fundamental driver point the same way, and a break of 108 opens air down to the 84.64 range low with no intervening structure.
key_risk: This is a conviction-2 position and its thinness is that there is no dated event forcing the outcome — the driver is a rolling geopolitical condition, and a Hormuz ceasefire or reopening headline gaps this short 10%-plus overnight with no chance to manage it. It is also not a diversifier: it is the same oil-higher bet the book already expresses long through XLE, DINO and DHT, so if oil rolls over, this loses at the same moment those do. Requires margin.
counter_argument: The bear case is fully public — UAL is already 22% off its high at roughly 12x the midpoint of its own reduced $7-11 guidance, airfares are up 26% year over year, and United is cutting about five points of scheduled capacity for the rest of 2026, which is exactly the discipline that protects pricing. Shorting a cyclical at 12x after the guidance cut has already happened, with zero insider selling signal beyond routine ($38.4M of sales, no buys), is late to a consensus trade.

catalyst.event: FOMC decision. Kalshi KXFEDDECISION-26SEP prices a 25bp HIKE at 57/58c against 41/42c for no change, on 5.3M and 9.6M contracts respectively; CME FedWatch reads 60.4%, up from ~56% before Chair Warsh recommitted to the 2% PCE target at Jackson Hole on 08/28 and said better summer inflation readings do not show underlying trends improving. The 08/30 Hormuz escalation put Brent at $90.91 and US gasoline above $4/gal for every day of August, which is the second- and third-order pressure the hawks need. Nearer term, the August jobs report lands Friday 09/04 08:30 ET against a 4.1% unemployment rate.
catalyst.action: Short into the 296.50-301.50 retest of the broken 50-day (297.28) and 20-day (300.14) averages, not at 293.93. Cover half at 274. If the 09/04 jobs report prints a rising unemployment rate the hike odds collapse and the trade is void — stand down rather than hold through it.

thesis: The Russell 2000 is the index with the most floating-rate debt and the largest share of unprofitable constituents, so it is the one that discounts a policy rate going up rather than down, and the market now assigns a 57-60% probability to a hike on 09/16 with the 2-year already at 4.34% versus a 3.63% effective funds rate. IWM has broken both its 20-day (300.14) and 50-day (297.28) averages and closed at 293.93 while the 200-day sits 7.6% lower at 271.56, so the level being defended has no support beneath it until that average.
key_risk: The instrument is a compromise and should be named as such: config/universe.md prefers /M2K over shorting IWM, but the Russell 2000 index level could not be fetched from any source this morning (finnhub refuses index CFDs, yahoo returned 429, stooq 404), and quoting contract levels I did not fetch would be a fabrication. So this is the ETF, and it requires margin. The trade also stacks with the SPY short already published at 773 — two index shorts is one macro bet expressed twice, and both die on the same headline.
counter_argument: A hike is 57% priced, not 0% priced, so the obvious part of this is in the price already, and IWM is only 3.7% off its 52-week high with ATR at 0.96% — this is an orderly pullback, not a breakdown. If the Fed holds, or if Treasury Secretary Bessent wins the public argument that you do not raise into a supply shock, small caps are the highest-beta thing to a relief rally and this short is the wrong side of a 5% gap.

catalyst.event: The scarce asset in this war is liquefaction capacity, not molecules. Iranian missiles hit Ras Laffan in March 2026 and took roughly 17% of Qatar export capacity offline; QatarEnergy force majeure on European and Asian supply has now been extended into October-November, and LNG through Hormuz is down about 95%. Onshore liquefaction takes five to six years to permit and build. Golar is the listed pure-play in floating liquefaction, which can be ordered and deployed on a fraction of that timeline.
catalyst.action: Accumulate on weakness, not here. Buy the first third into 46-47 (the 200-day sits at 47.05), the second third at 44, the last under 41. There is no urgency: the contracts are 20 years long and the entry matters more than the week. Do not chase 51.49.

thesis: At 51.49 the market cap is $5.23B on 101.76M shares and net debt was $1.60B at 2026-06-30 ($2.76B gross debt against $1.16B cash), so enterprise value is roughly $6.8B against management guidance of about $800M run-rate adjusted EBITDA by 2028 with Gimi, Hilli and Esperanza all operating — 8.6x, before any commodity upside, for cash flow contracted over twenty years. The contracts are real and already performing: Hilli signed a 20-year agreement with SESA in Argentina worth $285M a year of adjusted EBITDA to Golar plus a commodity-linked tariff of 25% of FOB prices, Hilli ran 100% uptime, and Gimi has delivered roughly 15-19% above its contracted base rate. The fourth Mark II unit ordered with CIMC Raffles lifts controlled capacity 41% to over 12 million tonnes, which is what takes the 2030 figure past $1.2B. Target 65 is 11x the 2028 number against an estimated $2.2B of net debt after the Mark II build.
key_risk: The valuation depends on capex I cannot pin down: Mark II delivery is guided to year-end 2027 and a fourth unit is now on order, so net debt rises from $1.60B before the 2028 EBITDA arrives, and my $2.2B assumption for 2028 is an estimate rather than a disclosed figure — if it lands nearer $3B the target is closer to 55 than 65. Explicit invalidation: Mark II slipping beyond 2028, the SESA Argentina contract failing to reach commercial operation, or an equity raise to fund the fourth unit. Golar is a foreign private issuer, so the zero insider transactions in six months carries no information either way rather than being a neutral signal.
counter_argument: Golar has spent a decade promising that the next unit is the one that re-rates it, and the shares are still 10.9% below their own 12-month high at 57.79 in the middle of the largest LNG supply shock on record — which is the market saying it does not believe the 2028 number. Argentina is the counterparty for the anchor contract, a jurisdiction with a long history of renegotiating energy economics, and a Hormuz reopening compresses the global spread that makes marginal liquefaction valuable in the first place.
